title: The Funding Paradox in U.S. Nonprofits
description: More nonprofits exist than ever, but average funding per organization is declining.

slides.headline: The Funding Paradox
slides.subheadline: More nonprofits exist. But are they getting funded?

slides.label: Part 1: The Trend
slides.headline: Growth Without Matching Funding
slides.story: The nonprofit sector grew by 180,000+ organizations in a decade. Sounds like victory. But here's the catch: average funding per nonprofit declined 3%. We added organizations—but diluted the funding pool. The pie didn't grow. It was divided more ways.

slides.label: Part 2: Who Gets Squeezed
slides.headline: Small Nonprofits Compete Harder for Less
slides.accent_label: Small Nonprofits with Declining Funding Access
slides.story: Organizations under $500K face the most pressure. More competitors. Same donor dollars. Less visibility. No marketing budget. They do incredible work but get squeezed by pure competition. Donors have no way to identify which small orgs are actually thriving.

slides.label: Part 3: The Answer
slides.headline: Data Directs Funding Where It Works
slides.story: Funders who use financial data identify strong small nonprofits others miss. You see resilience, not just scale. You fund impact, not visibility. Strategic funding based on real data changes outcomes. That's leverage.

slides.headline: Fund Smarter. Fund Smaller.
body_lines: See which nonprofits are actually thriving.
